conversation.message: I was wondering about different types of cameras. What are the main differences between a DSLR and a mirrorless camera?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: DSLRs typically use a mirror mechanism to reflect light to an optical viewfinder, while mirrorless cameras send light directly to the sensor for an electronic viewfinder or LCD screen. This often makes mirrorless cameras more compact and lighter.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: DSLRs often use phase-detection autofocus for speed, while mirrorless cameras use a combination of phase and contrast detection, which can be more precise. Lens availability also varies, with DSLRs having a longer history and therefore a wider range of older lenses.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Yes, the autofocus system definitely impacts low-light performance; mirrorless cameras often excel here due to their on-sensor phase detection. The availability of specialized lenses also plays a role in optimizing low-light shooting.
